note: The Gambia, read on 2026-10-30 in FactCheck Gambia's explainer on acquiring a residence permit (27 August 2024), which quotes section 10(2) of the Immigration Act 1965 (amended 2004) and describes the three permits the Gambia Immigration Department issues, and in The Point's report of the 2023 budget speech (5 December 2022), quoting the Minister of Finance. Both are secondary; the Department's own site (gid.gov.gm) and the Act's text weren't reachable today. Under s. 10(2) a residential permit states whether it is for residence only or for residence and employment, and a residence-only permit is subject to the holder having sufficient means to live without employment. Type A is for residence only, issued mainly to retired foreigners and students: written as the means route allowing no work. Type B is for residence and employment, issued to ECOWAS citizens and to skilled foreign workers; Type C is also for employment, issued to unskilled workers, especially from ECOWAS states: both written as work routes, the explainer not saying whether they tie their holder to an employer, so `work` is left out of them. 'Residential permits are renewed annually': written as a one-year term, renewable. No fee is written: the explainer's list (from January 2024) and the budget speech's (ECOWAS permit A D1,850 to D3,000, ECOWAS permit B D1,850 to D2,500, non-ECOWAS permit B D3,100 to D5,000, the alien card D1,500 to D2,500) don't agree on which permit costs what, and the form holds one fee where the speech gives one for ECOWAS citizens and another for others. The explainer says citizens of Mauritania, Guinea, Mali and Senegal are exempted by law from paying for the permit, and that applications go to a Gambian embassy or to the Department in Banjul (so `apply` isn't fixed). Nothing is said of decision times, permanent residence or naturalisation's years.

sources.title: FactCheck Gambia, EXPLAINER: How to Acquire a Residence Permit in Gambia (27 August 2024)
sources.said: According to section 10 (2) of the Immigration Act, 1965 (amended in 2004), a residential permit issued to an individual shall indicate whether the permit is for residence only or for residence and employment. However, the issueance of a residence only permit is subject to the fact that one has sufficient means to live in The Gambia without gainful employment. ... there are 3 categories of residential permits issued by The Gambia Immigration Department. These include types A, B, and C: ... Is is for residence purpose only and it is issued mainly to retired foreign citizens and international students. ... Is for residence and employment purposes. Citizens of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and other foreign nationals who are skilled workers are issued with this type of residence permit. ... This residential permit is also for employment purposes and is issued to unskilled workers, especially those from ECOWAS member states. ... However, citizens of Mauritania, the Republic of Guinea, Mali, and Senegal are exempted by law from paying for the resident permit. ... Residential permits are renewed annually.
